annotation.title_clean: Autonomous Shipyard Robots; Ethical Issues with Using AI in Power Systems
annotation.title_en: Autonomous Shipyard Robots; Ethical Issues with Using AI in Power Systems
annotation.venue: University of Virginia Libra Online Archive (School of Engineering and Applied Science, BS thesis)
annotation.summary_en: Undergraduate thesis abstract combining a technical project on lightweight vision-language-action models for autonomous shipyard robots with an STS literature review on AI bias, data insecurity and accountability in power systems, using an ethics-of-care lens and urging transparent, uniform mitigation and updated energy policy.
key_provisions_or_claims: Lightweight VLA models are promising for hazardous shipyard tasks but need substantial training data.
Mitigation measures for AI issues should be transparent and uniformly implemented.
Energy regulations and policies must change to account for AI-induced impacts.
An ethics-of-care approach should guide AI deployment in power systems.
Energy-efficient AI models should be further evaluated.
